target: Repair the blocked Windows 2.19.0 collector installation without changing archive, summary, cloud, or capture semantics.
primary_semantics: Every InteractiveToken collector task binds an explicit current Windows UserId from the shared Platform identity owner, and registration failures retain their native diagnostic in the rollback journal.
invariants: Raw archives, summaries, indexes, cloud state, configuration, cursors, and the active archive-root pointer are not rewritten by this repair.
The collector remains a direct hidden native Task Scheduler action with LeastPrivilege and exactly one startup owner.
A failed installation restores the previous generation and preserves the native task-registration diagnostic.
The installed generation is accepted only after a real Windows task query, process identity check, and archive-watermark advance.
The existing canonical owner remains authoritative; this repair introduces no additive bypass and cannot regress an earlier passing case that shares the scheduler or installer boundary.
allowed_changes: Use the shared Platform Windows identity owner when rendering the existing collector task principal.
Capture native schtasks output in the existing transactional rollback error.
Update patch-version metadata, documentation, regression tests, receipts, package evidence, and release assets.
prohibited_changes: Add a Run-key fallback, second scheduler, wrapper process, alternate installer, or competing startup owner.
Change Summary V2 rescue, archive formats, capture selection, cloud protocols, dashboard behavior, or maintenance policy.
Treat mock tests, package construction, installer exit zero, or process existence alone as installed-effect proof.
before_after_checks: Verify generated and queried task XML contain the same nonempty UserId, direct native command, hidden setting, and LeastPrivilege policy.
Verify a registration failure records native stderr and rolls back without changing the active archive-root pointer.
Upgrade the existing 2.15.0 installation through the packaged installer and verify one task, one installed collector generation, fresh telemetry, shortcut identity, and archive-watermark progress.
Verify Python, Rust, documentation, and packaged binary versions all report 2.19.1.

original_triggers: The released 2.19.0 installer returned an outer exit code of zero while its hidden install transaction rolled back after schtasks rejected the collector task XML.
The collector installer duplicated Principal XML and omitted UserId even though the shared Platform scheduler already owned correct Windows identity rendering.
FakeRunner accepted malformed platform XML, so package and mock evidence escaped without a real Windows Task Scheduler effect check.
